transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, what really brought me in is that I seem to be having trouble absorbing what people say to me. 

Like, my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or coordinating his rides, and I’m looking right at her... but a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. It happens a lot, and it's starting to cause some friction.
Have you experienced these kinds of difficulties with focus and attention since you were a child, or is this a relatively new development in your life?

It's definitely not new. I've been like this since I was a kid. Even back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but that I was just always daydreaming. 

I would do my homework and then leave it sitting right inside my desk, and they constantly had to give me reminders to actually finish my classwork. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
